digest.component_or_area: cache and temp artifact write safety
propositions: Six sites derive temp file names from content hashes, pid, or fixed suffixes, creating collision hazards across concurrent writers; two of these sites lack atomic writes altogether, allowing torn reads.
The existing fsutil.atomic_write helper implements the required pattern (mkstemp, write, chmod, replace) and is already in use at ~50 call sites but not at the six identified hazards.

A full audit of src/rebar cache and temp write sites yielded zero root-unkeyed caches (all use absolute path, repo root, or stat token keying) and confirmed six shared-name hazards, with the negative result to be documented.
Converting all six hazard sites to use fsutil.atomic_write, and making the two previously non-atomic sites atomic, eliminates the shared temp collision and torn-read windows.
A two-writer concurrency regression test using threading.Barrier and monkeypatch.setattr on os.replace must pass on converted code and fail on the original shared-name pattern.
